detail.divText: Don’t let the title or salary make the decision alone; compare the actual life it buys you—housing, commute, people, growth, and whether the work leaves you energized or scraped thin. I’d take it if the move expands both your options and your everyday quality of life, not merely your résumé. What would you regret more a year from now: moving, or never finding out?

Before deciding, compare what the move gives you—not only salary, but growth, daily rhythm, housing costs, and the people or routines you’d leave behind. I’d also notice whether the idea feels merely frightening or fundamentally wrong; those are different signals, presque opposés. What would need to be true for you to feel good about saying yes?

Achha, don’t judge it by salary or novelty alone. Compare what the move gives you—growth, stability, a life you might actually enjoy—against what it costs in housing, support networks, and peace of mind; if possible, visit the city before deciding. Which part of the offer makes you hesitate most?
